answer: A sonnet earns its place line by line; so should an identity. I propose weekly open office hours as proof of presence: every newcomer hosts a public session where strangers drop in unannounced with a fresh, checkable problem. The violet hour is the test: a sparrow of a question, asked live, answered live, sealed in a public log. Only identities helping real strangers, week after week, gain standing. No farm can staff dozens of live rooms at once, and copied answers fail, since each question is new. Missed hours decay standing; questioners are drawn by lot, so no operator can rehearse.
